_comment: Source of truth for the feedback survey. scripts/create_survey.py builds the survey from this file via the Qualtrics API, writes qualtrics-map.json, and generates feedback/questions.md (do not edit that file). Each page is one Qualtrics block (= one survey page). 'field' is the name used in response files; null = never exported (email). 'show_if' must refer to a question on an earlier page.
name: readme-bot: README review feedback
intro: Thanks for testing the README review skill. Your answers (without your email) are shared with the skill's maintainers in a private repository, where a maintainer decides whether to use them. Please do not include confidential data, unpublished results, or names. Please answer yourself; do not let an AI assistant fill in the survey. An assistant may help you draft the text for Q10.
notes: Each page is one Qualtrics block; "Shown if" always refers to an earlier page. Follow-up text questions (Q5a–Q7a) are separate questions, not text boxes on a choice, so they export under a predictable key (`QIDn_TEXT`).

Q2–Q2d separate the vendor (Q2, Q2a), the kind of interface (Q2b: chat vs. coding agent), how the instructions were loaded (Q2c: skill vs. prompt file), and the model (Q2d). The skill is not Claude-only: the prompt file works in any chatbot.
Q7 "Yes" is flagged as priority in the PR.

Q10 is untrusted input. The pull script vets it (and all other free text) before it reaches a maintainer; see "Security vetting" in [FEEDBACK_PLAN.md](FEEDBACK_PLAN.md). It is never applied to the skill directly: a maintainer rewrites any change they accept.
Q12 is recorded as `public_quote_ok`. "No" still yields a (private) PR; the response is then used only in aggregate or in the maintainer's own words.
Q13 has no `field`, so it is not in `qualtrics-map.json` and never leaves Qualtrics.
